_about: Generic per-family guidance used when there is no researched profile for the exact part. Ranges are deliberately conservative starting points, not measurements: Headroom's own tests decide the final values. Run 'Research my hardware' (Setup) for model-specific results with sources.

nvidia-blackwell.label: NVIDIA RTX 50 series (Blackwell)
nvidia-blackwell.tuning_method: Core + memory clock offsets via NVML. No voltage change; the card's firmware keeps its power limit.

notes: GDDR7 corrects errors by retrying, so an unstable memory offset shows up as LOWER bandwidth before it crashes. Headroom stops the memory search when bandwidth stops improving.

nvidia-ada.label: NVIDIA RTX 40 series (Ada Lovelace)
nvidia-ada.tuning_method: Core + memory clock offsets via NVML. No voltage change; the card's firmware keeps its power limit.

notes: Ada cards usually run close to their limit out of the box; gains are smaller than on RTX 50.

nvidia-ampere.label: NVIDIA RTX 30 series (Ampere)
nvidia-ampere.tuning_method: Core + memory clock offsets via NVML. No voltage change; the card's firmware keeps its power limit.

notes: GDDR6X cards (3070 Ti/3080/3090) run hot memory; check the VRAM temperature in the Fans tab and keep the fan curve's VRAM side up.

nvidia-turing.label: NVIDIA RTX 20 / GTX 16 series (Turing)
nvidia-turing.tuning_method: Core + memory clock offsets via NVML, if the driver allows it on this card.

nvidia-workstation.label: NVIDIA workstation / data-centre GPU
nvidia-workstation.tuning_method: Not tuned: workstation cards are validated at stock clocks. Monitoring and fan curve only.

nvidia-other.label: Other NVIDIA GPU
nvidia-other.tuning_method: Core + memory clock offsets via NVML, very conservative limits.

amd.label: AMD Radeon
amd.tuning_method: Not supported yet: Headroom's GPU tuning uses NVIDIA's NVML. Use AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition > Performance > Tuning (try 'Undervolt GPU' first).

intel.label: Intel Arc / integrated graphics
intel.tuning_method: Not supported: use Intel Graphics Software > Performance tuning.

amd-zen5-x3d.label: AMD Ryzen 9000X3D (Zen 5 + 3D V-Cache)
amd-zen5-x3d.tuning_method: PBO + per-core negative Curve Optimizer (found by CoreCycler) + Max Boost Clock Override. Power limits stay stock.

notes: Don't raise PPT/TDC/EDC: the cache makes games barely clock-sensitive, so it only adds heat.
Keep SoC voltage at or below 1.20 V (EXPO profiles can push it higher).
Ryzen 9000 often freezes instead of rebooting on a bad Curve Optimizer value: press reset; CoreCycler resumes and raises that core by 1.

amd-zen5.label: AMD Ryzen 9000 (Zen 5)
amd-zen5.tuning_method: PBO + per-core negative Curve Optimizer (found by CoreCycler) + Max Boost Clock Override. Power limits stay stock.

notes: Headroom never raises PPT/TDC/EDC. On 65 W parts (9600X/9700X) most extra multi-thread performance would come from higher power limits, which Headroom deliberately leaves to you.
Ryzen 9000 often freezes instead of rebooting on a bad Curve Optimizer value: press reset; CoreCycler resumes and raises that core by 1.

amd-zen4-x3d.label: AMD Ryzen 7000X3D (Zen 4 + 3D V-Cache)
amd-zen4-x3d.tuning_method: Per-core negative Curve Optimizer only (found by CoreCycler). These chips don't allow a boost clock override.

notes: Keep SoC voltage at or below 1.30 V; update the BIOS (2023 BIOS updates capped it after socket damage reports).

amd-zen4.label: AMD Ryzen 7000 (Zen 4)
amd-zen4.tuning_method: PBO + per-core negative Curve Optimizer (found by CoreCycler) + Max Boost Clock Override. Power limits stay stock.

notes: Zen 4 is designed to run up to 95 C under heavy load; Headroom's 85 C limit is a quieter, cooler target.

amd-zen3.label: AMD Ryzen 5000 (Zen 3)
amd-zen3.tuning_method: PBO + per-core negative Curve Optimizer (found by CoreCycler) + Max Boost Clock Override. Power limits stay stock.

amd-zen3-x3d.label: AMD Ryzen 5000X3D (Zen 3 + 3D V-Cache)
amd-zen3-x3d.tuning_method: Per-core negative Curve Optimizer only (if your BIOS exposes it); no boost override.

amd-zen2.label: AMD Ryzen 3000 (Zen 2)
amd-zen2.tuning_method: Not supported: Curve Optimizer doesn't exist on Zen 2. Monitoring and benchmark only.

intel-raptorlake.label: Intel Core 13th/14th gen (Raptor Lake)
intel-raptorlake.tuning_method: No automatic tuning. Most important: update the BIOS to the latest microcode (0x12B or newer) and use Intel's default power profile, which fixes the 13th/14th gen degradation issue.

notes: Do not raise voltage or power limits on 13th/14th gen.

intel-arrowlake.label: Intel Core Ultra 200S (Arrow Lake)
intel-arrowlake.tuning_method: No automatic tuning. Intel's '200S Boost' BIOS profile (where offered) is the supported overclock and keeps the warranty.

other.label: Other CPU
other.tuning_method: No automatic tuning. Monitoring and benchmark only.

asus.label: ASUS
asus.pbo_path: Advanced > AMD Overclocking > (Accept) > Precision Boost Overdrive

msi.label: MSI
msi.pbo_path: OC > Advanced CPU Configuration > AMD Overclocking > Precision Boost Overdrive

gigabyte.label: Gigabyte
gigabyte.pbo_path: Tweaker > Advanced CPU Settings > Precision Boost Overdrive (or Settings > AMD Overclocking)
gigabyte.thermal_limit_name: Platform Thermal Throttle Limit / Thermal Limit

asrock.label: ASRock
asrock.pbo_path: Advanced > AMD Overclocking > Precision Boost Overdrive (or OC Tweaker)
